title: How long a film before reading runs
statement: How long a film before a reading should run is not settled: a rule, a worked example and a built lesson each give it a different length.
example: One rule caps an intro film at 30 to 40 seconds, while a built lesson's film runs 1:54.
detail: One version of the intro-video rules holds that an intro video is 30 to 40 seconds and a longer one is weaker, a number derived from the film's shape of five or six shots of one spoken line each (`downloads/BrainLift - What makes a good intro video.md`, line 87). The other compresses a script of about three minutes to about 60 seconds in its worked example (lines 361-363), and a built Grade 3 lesson opens with a 1:54 film (`downloads/SUPERSEDED — see v2 (table format)_ WITW Lesson 1 learning walkthrough.md`, line 25). The short rule itself notes that educational video practice, measured on lectures, has engagement holding for several minutes (line 87, citing Guo, Kim and Rubin 2014).
against: The short rule's own source calls it the least evidenced claim it holds, derived from the film's shape and not measured on children (`downloads/BrainLift - What makes a good intro video.md`, line 87).
